relevance_note: Case-control study of four Japanese women with LCAT abnormalities, each shown individually in Figures 1 and 2 ("a patient with familial LCAT deficiency"; "patient #1 with fish-eye disease"), so individual-level detail (sex, diagnosis, corneal opacity) is available, though thin.
method_note: Written by hand with a short Python script for assembly. The paper reports only group-level data (medians, IQRs, percentages) for its four LCAT-group patients; per-person facts come from the Figure 1 and Figure 2 legends (diagnosis per panel) and statements naming the whole LCAT group (all women; all presented with cloudy corneas; 'Patients with LCAT deficiency and fish-eye disease ... show decreased contrast sensitivity at most spatial frequencies'). The FLD patient has no label ('a patient with familial LCAT deficiency') and is 'unnamed person 1'; FED patients use the paper's labels 'patient #1'-'#3'. Not assigned to individuals (counts without names): photophobia in 3 of 4 (75%, n = 3), subjective deterioration of vision in 1 of 4, decreased contrast sensitivity in seven of eight eyes, and group medians for age, BCVA, astigmatism, straylight, corneal thickness, IOP, phakia. Diagnosis required 'confirmation via genetic analysis', so one LCAT variant row per person is kept with variant_original_string 'not reported' (no variant printed; number of alleles per person unknown). Ethnicity 'Japanese' is taken from the title (group). Reference [11] (Ono 2020, same authors and hospital) is cited for the diagnostic approach only; the paper does not state that these patients were reported before, so cites_prior_report is left null. cohort_size_as_stated counts only the four LCAT-group patients; the four healthy controls are out of scope. Inconsistency: the Abstract says 'two with FLD and six with FED' (eyes) while Results say three FED patients and one FLD patient (consistent in eyes). Exclusion criteria (no corneal surgery etc.) were not used as evidence.
